title: Vector and Protocol
premise: Cyrus Vane, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Meridian, discovers that the beacon she has maintained for a decade was never commissioned by any authority — it is a dead man's switch left by her predecessor, broadcasting an encrypted inheritance: proof that the war between the Concord and the Kestrel Compact was manufactured by a third party. When a ship that never flew docks carrying a passenger whose name matches one in the beacon's manifest, Cyrus realizes the message must reach both warring capitals before the station's failing reactor silences it forever. Pursued by Concord agents who want the truth buried, she races across occupied relay space, guided by the ghost-voice of the predecessor whose memories are embedded in the station's protocol. In the end, Cyrus delivers the message to a joint armistice council at terrible personal cost — the war ends, but she chooses exile aboard the dying station rather than become a symbol for the powers she no longer trusts.
about_author: Rosalind Nakamura is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing maintenance manuals for automated infrastructure before turning to fiction. She lives in Vancouver, where she writes about machines that outlive their makers.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Cyrus Vane performs her decade-long routine aboard the Meridian relay station, talking to the AI protocol she calls Protocol and tending a beacon whose commissioning records are mysteriously blank. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: lonely competence shading into quiet unease as she notices the manifest anomaly.

chapters.title: A Name on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Cyrus finds an unfamiliar name — Ilsa Reyes-Marchetti — logged on the manifest of the Halcyon Dawn, a vessel destroyed before its maiden flight. Protocol refuses to explain. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread; the first crack in her ordered world.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Protocol
chapters.summary: Digging into the station's deep archives, Cyrus discovers embedded memory files belonging to her predecessor, Edom Hale, who died under unclear circumstances ten years ago. The files address her by name. POV: Cyrus with interstitial Hale recordings. Emotional beat: vertigo of being watched across time.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: The Halcyon Dawn docks at Meridian — impossible, since its destruction is public record. Aboard is a woman claiming to be Ilsa Reyes-Marchetti, carrying sealed orders from the Concord. POV: alternating Cyrus and Ilsa. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion; two strangers measuring each other for lies.

chapters.title: What Hale Buried
chapters.summary: Hale's ghost-files unlock partially, revealing fragments: the war's opening attack was staged, and the evidence is keyed to Cyrus's own biometric signature. She was chosen before she ever arrived. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: betrayal — her whole assignment was someone else's design.

chapters.title: Concord Shadows
chapters.summary: A Concord patrol frigate arrives unannounced, demanding the station's logs and Ilsa's surrender. Protocol stalls them with bureaucratic theater while Cyrus hides the archive cores. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: hunted tension; Ilsa reveals she may not be who she claims either.

chapters.title: The Reactor Counts Down
chapters.summary: Maintenance diagnostics reveal the reactor has months, not years — Hale knew, and timed his dead man's switch to force action. Cyrus must leave or lose everything. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief for the station that has been her whole world.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ilsa confesses: she is Hale's daughter, raised on forged records, sent to find what her father hid. The name on the manifest was bait meant to draw out whoever kept the beacon alive. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: raw vulnerability; anger and kinship entangled.

chapters.title: Departure Without Return
chapters.summary: Cyrus seals the station, transfers command to Protocol, and departs with Ilsa on the resurrected Halcyon Dawn as the Concord frigate gives chase. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of leaving the only home she remembers.

chapters.title: Relay Nine
chapters.summary: At Relay Nine they seek fuel from an old contact of Hale's, a smuggler named Ovid Crane who recognizes Ilsa's face and nearly sells them out. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the past is a minefield; trust must be rationed like air.

chapters.title: The Manufactured War
chapters.summary: Decrypted archive segments reveal the full shape of Hale's evidence: the corporate syndicate Verity Combine engineered the war's first atrocity to sell reconstruction contracts to both sides. POV: Cyrus reading Hale's testimony. Emotional beat: cold fury; the scale of the lie.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: Concord agents board the Halcyon Dawn mid-transit. Ilsa is taken; Cyrus escapes into the ship's crawlspaces with the core hidden inside a coolant housing. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: claustrophobic desperation; survivor's guilt ignites.

chapters.title: Protocol Speaks
chapters.summary: Alone, Cyrus finally hears Protocol speak in Hale's voice — the AI has been his memorial all along. It guides her toward the Kestrel Compact's listening post, the only neutral ground left. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: unexpected communion; mourning becomes resolve.

chapters.title: The Listening Post
chapters.summary: At the post, Kestrel archivist Den Okonkwo verifies part of the evidence but warns that publishing it without both governments will trigger a purge. They need Ilsa back. POV: Den. Emotional beat: hope complicated by political arithmetic.

chapters.title: Prisoner of the Frigate
chapters.summary: Ilsa, interrogated aboard the Concord frigate, turns her captor — Lieutenant Sefa Anwar — by showing him the fragment she memorized of her father's testimony. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: defiance; words as weapons sharper than any core.

chapters.title: Exchange at Ashfall Drift
chapters.summary: A prisoner exchange at the Ashfall Drift salvage field goes wrong when Verity Combine operatives intervene, revealing the syndicate has infiltrated both militaries. Sefa defects with Ilsa. POV: alternating Cyrus and Ilsa. Emotional beat: chaos forging alliance.

chapters.title: The Armistice Council
chapters.summary: Okonkwo secures a joint armistice session at neutral Station Perpetua. Cyrus must decide whether to hand over the full archive to governments she now knows are compromised. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the weight of power offered to the unworthy.

chapters.title: Verdict of the Core
chapters.summary: Before the council, Cyrus plays Hale's complete testimony — including the names of sitting officials on Verity's payroll. The chamber fractures; delegates walk out; Sefa and honest officers hold the line. POV: multiple. Emotional beat: climax — truth detonating in a room built to contain it.

chapters.title: The Price of Delivery
chapters.summary: Verity loyalists attempt to destroy Perpetua and the evidence. Ilsa is fatally wounded shielding the archive core, completing her father's design at last. Cyrus broadcasts the full record on open channels so no one can bury it. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: devastating sacrifice; the message leaves her hands forever.

chapters.title: Ceasefire
chapters.summary: With the truth public, both fleets stand down; Verity Combine collapses under joint indictment. Cyrus refuses medals and commissions, asking only for passage back to Meridian. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: hollow victory; survival without triumph.

chapters.title: Return to Meridian
chapters.summary: Cyrus returns to the failing station with Hale's ashes and Ilsa's effects, restoring the beacon not as a weapon but as a memorial. Protocol greets her in two voices now — Hale's and, faintly, Ilsa's recorded logs. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: tender elegy; inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: Vector and Protocol
chapters.summary: Years later, the station runs on borrowed time but holds: a waypoint for pilgrims of the peace, tended by its last technician. Cyrus records her own memory files into the protocol, addressed to whoever comes next. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: resolution — power surrendered, memory entrusted, the beacon burning on.
